note: A = outgoing shot, B = incoming shot

transitions.name: Hard Cut
transitions.how: 1 Choose the end point of A and the start point of B. 2 Remove the gap and butt them together. 3 Check eyeline, action and sound.
transitions.use_when: Dialogue, documentary, information-dense content
transitions.effect: Clean and direct; keeps the narrative pace.
transitions.prompt: Hard cut from the end of A straight to B, keep the action continuous, no transition effect.
transitions.pitfalls: Make sure the shot logic works first.

transitions.name: Cut on Action
transitions.how: 1 Find a cut point mid-action. 2 Bring B in on the continuation of the same action. 3 Trim frame by frame to remove repeated or missing motion.
transitions.use_when: Opening doors, turning, picking things up, sport
transitions.effect: Uses movement to lead the eye so the cut goes unnoticed.
transitions.prompt: Cut from A mid-way through raising the hand to B continuing the motion; match direction and speed.
transitions.pitfalls: Action phase and screen axis must match.

transitions.name: Graphic Match
transitions.how: 1 Pick similar silhouettes. 2 Align position, scale and rotation. 3 Cut where the compositions are closest.
transitions.use_when: Brand logos, round objects, cross-era storytelling
transitions.effect: Creates a visual link or metaphor.
transitions.prompt: Align the round subject in A with the round subject in B, match size, then hard cut.
transitions.pitfalls: Keep the subject's position identical; avoid extra distortion.

transitions.name: Color Match
transitions.how: 1 Find shots with a similar dominant colour. 2 Correct colour temperature and brightness. 3 Cut to B when the same colour fills the frame.
transitions.use_when: Fashion, food, travel, brand colours
transitions.effect: Keeps colour continuity across scenes.
transitions.prompt: Hard cut when A and B share the same dominant colour; unify brightness and colour temperature.
transitions.pitfalls: Colour matching is not the same as applying one LUT to both shots.

transitions.name: Motion Match
transitions.how: 1 Find movement in the same direction. 2 Align speed and subject position. 3 Cut where the motion phases are closest.
transitions.use_when: Throws and catches, rotating products, sports montages
transitions.effect: Joins different scenes into one continuous momentum.
transitions.prompt: A moving right cuts to B moving right; match speed and subject position, then cut.
transitions.pitfalls: Can cross scenes; different from a continuity cut on the same action.

transitions.name: Jump Cut
transitions.how: 1 Use footage from the same camera position. 2 Remove pauses or intervening time. 3 Keep the intentional jump in pose.
transitions.use_when: Talking-head videos, tutorials, time compression
transitions.effect: Speeds things up and emphasises the passage of time.
transitions.prompt: Remove the pauses in A, keep same-angle jump cuts, and make the sentences flow naturally.
transitions.pitfalls: Accept the visible jump; don't clip the ends of words.

transitions.name: Smash / Contrast Cut
transitions.how: 1 Pick two segments with strong emotional or sonic contrast. 2 Hard cut on the reaction point. 3 Switch or cut the sound abruptly at the same moment.
transitions.use_when: Comedic reversals, waking from a dream, sharp mood shifts
transitions.effect: Creates surprise, irony or impact.
transitions.prompt: Hard cut from the loudest moment of A to the silence of B; the sound stops at the same instant.
transitions.pitfalls: The story should justify the contrast; don't do it just to show off.

transitions.name: Cutaway
transitions.how: 1 Insert a relevant detail over the edit point in A. 2 Keep the original dialogue playing continuously. 3 Cut back to the main shot or into B.
transitions.use_when: Removing lines from interviews, tutorials, documentary
transitions.effect: Hides the jump cut and adds information.
transitions.prompt: Insert related detail shot B over the removed line in A; keep the dialogue continuous.
transitions.pitfalls: This is a shot-structure technique, not a software effect.

transitions.name: J-cut
transitions.how: 1 Split the audio and video edit points. 2 Let B's sound start before B's picture. 3 Balance levels across the handover.
transitions.use_when: Interviews, arriving at a new location, suspenseful teasers
transitions.effect: Uses sound to set up the viewer's expectation.
transitions.prompt: Bring B's audio in 0.5 s early, then cut from A to B's picture.
transitions.pitfalls: Requires an independently editable B audio track.

transitions.name: L-cut
transitions.how: 1 Cut the picture to B first. 2 Let A's dialogue or ambience continue. 3 Fade out A's audio at a natural sentence end.
transitions.use_when: Interview reaction shots, voice-over over B-roll
transitions.effect: Preserves emotional and semantic continuity.
transitions.prompt: Cut to B's picture first; let A's dialogue continue to the end of the sentence, then fade out.
transitions.pitfalls: Avoid A's audio masking B's dialogue.

transitions.name: Sound Bridge
transitions.how: 1 Pick a sound that can carry across scenes. 2 Lay it over the picture cut. 3 Mix in B's ambience.
transitions.use_when: Cross-location montages, flashbacks, thematic links
transitions.effect: Connects two spaces through sound.
transitions.prompt: Carry the same rain sound from A into B, gradually mixing in B's new ambience.
transitions.pitfalls: Related to J/L-cuts but doesn't require dialogue.

transitions.name: Cross Dissolve
transitions.how: 1 Keep extra handles on both clips. 2 Overlap A's tail with B's head. 3 Fade A's opacity down and B's up; check for ghosting.
transitions.use_when: Passage of time, memories, calm landscapes
transitions.effect: Soft transition that implies a time relationship.
transitions.prompt: 0.6 s cross dissolve from A to B with steady exposure.
transitions.pitfalls: Two overlapping faces can produce messy ghosting.

transitions.name: Dip to Black
transitions.how: 1 Fade A down to black. 2 Optionally hold on black briefly. 3 Bring B up from black to normal exposure.
transitions.use_when: End of a chapter, large time jumps, section breaks
transitions.effect: Creates a pause and a clear sense of sections.
transitions.prompt: Fade A to black over 0.3 s, then fade into B over 0.3 s.
transitions.pitfalls: Frequent dips to black can be mistaken for the ending.

transitions.name: Flash / Dip to White
transitions.how: 1 Brighten A's tail. 2 Cut to B at peak white. 3 Bring B back to normal exposure quickly.
transitions.use_when: Camera flashes, memory triggers, music beats
transitions.effect: Instant impact that masks the scene change.
transitions.prompt: Flash A to white then cut to B, return to normal exposure within 0.2 s, flash only once.
transitions.pitfalls: Avoid repeated full-screen flashing.

transitions.name: Luma Fade
transitions.how: 1 Stack A and B. 2 Use A's luminance as a matte. 3 Animate the threshold so B appears through light and dark areas in turn.
transitions.use_when: Skies, mountains, high-contrast silhouettes
transitions.effect: Reveals in layers that follow the image structure; richer than a plain dissolve.
transitions.prompt: Reveal B through A from highlights to shadows; 0.6 s luma fade.
transitions.pitfalls: Low-contrast footage needs threshold and edge softness adjusted.

transitions.name: Light Leak
transitions.how: 1 Place light-leak footage above both clips. 2 Use Screen or Add blending. 3 Align the brightest point with the cut, then fade out.
transitions.use_when: Weddings, travel, retro lifestyle
transitions.effect: Warm glow and film texture.
transitions.prompt: Overlay one warm light leak at the A-to-B cut, peak covering the cut, 0.5 s.
transitions.pitfalls: The leak should feel like a change in light and must not cover key information.

transitions.name: Film Burn
transitions.how: 1 Add a burn texture or procedural effect. 2 Expand bright edges and an irregular matte. 3 Burn through A to reveal B.
transitions.use_when: Retro music videos, flashbacks, film-look ads
transitions.effect: Organic, gritty material change.
transitions.prompt: A is overtaken by a warm film burn from the edges, revealing B after 0.5 s.
transitions.pitfalls: Unlike a uniform flash, it needs an irregular texture.

transitions.name: Whip Pan
transitions.how: 1 End A with a fast whip to the right. 2 Start B whipping in from the same direction. 3 Cut at peak blur and add a short whoosh.
transitions.use_when: Travel, sport, fast-paced B-roll
transitions.effect: Fast lateral momentum that hides the cut.
transitions.prompt: A whips right into B whipping in from the same direction; cut at peak motion blur.
transitions.pitfalls: Same direction, similar speed and exposure; plan it at the shoot when possible.

transitions.name: Occlusion Cut
transitions.how: 1 Push A into a hand or dark object. 2 Wait until the frame is fully covered. 3 Cut to B emerging from the same occlusion.
transitions.use_when: Outfit changes, space travel, fake one-takes
transitions.effect: The cut is hidden inside the occlusion.
transitions.prompt: Cut to B when A is fully covered by black clothing; B continues out from behind the same occlusion.
transitions.pitfalls: Must truly fill the frame; match movement and occluder colour.

transitions.name: Object Wipe
transitions.how: 1 Put B below A. 2 Track the edge of a foreground object passing through A. 3 Animate a mask along that edge to reveal B.
transitions.use_when: Passing pillars, vehicles, pedestrians, door frames
transitions.effect: The scene looks naturally wiped away by a foreground object.
transitions.prompt: Track the pillar moving left to right in A and use its edge to wipe in B.
transitions.pitfalls: Check mask edges and motion blur frame by frame.

transitions.name: Subject Mask
transitions.how: 1 Duplicate and cut out the subject. 2 Put the subject layer on top. 3 Change the background to B first, then hand over the subject.
transitions.use_when: Personal promos, product ads, fashion
transitions.effect: The subject stays continuous while the space around it changes abruptly.
transitions.prompt: Keep A's subject in the foreground, wipe the background to B, then hand over naturally to B's subject.
transitions.pitfalls: Hair, transparent objects and overlaps need edge cleanup.

transitions.name: Zoom In
transitions.how: 1 Align both shots' anchor points on the same spot. 2 Rapidly scale up A's tail with radial blur. 3 Bring B back from the zoomed state.
transitions.use_when: Product details, travel landmarks, beat-synced short videos
transitions.effect: Pushes forward into the next shot.
transitions.prompt: Quickly push in on A around the subject's centre, cut to B at peak blur, settle within 0.4 s.
transitions.pitfalls: Align the visual centre first; don't reveal frame edges.

transitions.name: Zoom Out
transitions.how: 1 Rapidly scale down and blur A. 2 Bring B in at a larger scale. 3 Keep the pull-out direction consistent and return to normal framing.
transitions.use_when: Detail to wide, spatial reveals, brand films
transitions.effect: Releases from the detail into a larger space.
transitions.prompt: Quickly pull out of A into B's wide shot, keep centre and direction consistent, 0.4 s.
transitions.pitfalls: When shrinking A, fill the background or mirror-extend the edges.

transitions.name: Spin Transition
transitions.how: 1 Accelerate A rotating around its centre. 2 Cut to B at peak blur. 3 Decelerate B in the same direction until it settles.
transitions.use_when: Dance, sport, trend-driven ads
transitions.effect: Rotational energy and rhythmic impact.
transitions.prompt: A spins clockwise into B decelerating in the same direction, with motion blur, settling in 0.4 s.
transitions.pitfalls: Fill the frame edges; don't let the subject flip over for no reason.

transitions.name: Speed Ramp
transitions.how: 1 Set time-remapping keyframes. 2 Speed up A's tail and bring B in at the same speed. 3 Slow B down to normal or slow motion.
transitions.use_when: Sport, product B-roll, travel
transitions.effect: Highlights the peak of the action and lifts the pace.
transitions.prompt: Speed up the end of A, cut to B at peak speed, B smoothly slows to normal.
transitions.pitfalls: Source frame rate limits slow-mo quality; the speed curve is not a fixed template.

transitions.name: Defocus
transitions.how: 1 Rack A out of focus. 2 Bring B in on an out-of-focus head. 3 Rack B back into focus; lens blur can simulate it in post.
transitions.use_when: Dreams, emotion, soft product reveals
transitions.effect: Hides the scene change inside visual blur.
transitions.prompt: A gradually defocuses to full blur, cut to B, then refocus; 0.6 s total.
transitions.pitfalls: Match the colour blocks and brightness of both blurred frames.

transitions.name: Linear Blur
transitions.how: 1 Overlap A and B. 2 Ramp directional blur to a peak at the midpoint. 3 Dissolve to B and clear the blur.
transitions.use_when: Tech, sport, motion graphics
transitions.effect: Directional sense of speed.
transitions.prompt: 0.3 s horizontal blur dissolve from A to B, blurriest at the midpoint, sharp at both ends.
transitions.pitfalls: Unlike a real whip pan, it works with static shots.

transitions.name: Ripple
transitions.how: 1 Animate a ripple displacement. 2 Mix in B at the ripple peak. 3 Reduce the ripple until B is stable.
transitions.use_when: Dreams, memories, water themes, retro looks
transitions.effect: Space ripples like liquid.
transitions.prompt: A shows a gentle spreading ripple and transitions to B, stabilising within 0.6 s.
transitions.pitfalls: Large ripples distort faces.

transitions.name: Morph Cut
transitions.how: 1 Remove the pause. 2 Add a Morph Cut between two segments with similar poses. 3 After analysis, check mouth, eyes and background.
transitions.use_when: Locked-off interviews, single-speaker talks
transitions.effect: Reduces the visual jump caused by removing lines.
transitions.prompt: Add a short Morph Cut to the same-angle talking-head jump cut; keep mouth shape and background stable.
transitions.pitfalls: Not suitable for different people or large movements.

transitions.name: Glitch
transitions.how: 1 Add short RGB split and horizontal offset near the cut. 2 Cut to B in the middle. 3 Quickly return the effect to zero.
transitions.use_when: Esports, digital products, malfunction storylines
transitions.effect: Digital interference and instability.
transitions.prompt: Add a 0.2 s RGB split and horizontal glitch from A to B, then return to clean immediately.
transitions.pitfalls: Don't distort small text or brand logos for long.

transitions.name: Pixelize
transitions.how: 1 A's pixel blocks grow from fine to coarse. 2 Cut to B at the coarsest point. 3 B's blocks shrink back to sharp.
transitions.use_when: Gaming, tech, retro pixel style
transitions.effect: Digital break-down and reassembly.
transitions.prompt: Pixelate A into large blocks, cut to B, then return to sharp; 0.5 s total.
transitions.pitfalls: Not for frames where text must stay readable.

transitions.name: Slide / Push
transitions.how: 1 Lay A and B side by side. 2 Move both left by one screen at the same speed. 3 Ease B into place.
transitions.use_when: Tutorial steps, product features, info cards
transitions.effect: Clearly expresses sequence and spatial relationship.
transitions.prompt: A moves out to the left as B pushes in from the right in sync, easing in over 0.4 s.
transitions.pitfalls: Unlike a wipe, both images move.

transitions.name: Wipe
transitions.how: 1 Put B below A. 2 Sweep a straight-edge mask from left to right. 3 A is progressively replaced by B.
transitions.use_when: Chapter changes, charts, brand animation
transitions.effect: Replaces the image cleanly and crisply.
transitions.prompt: Replace A with B using a left-to-right linear wipe, 0.4 s, crisp edge.
transitions.pitfalls: The subject doesn't need to follow the wipe edge.

transitions.name: Iris
transitions.how: 1 Create a circular mask. 2 Centre it on the focal point. 3 Grow the radius from zero to full frame.
transitions.use_when: Playful, retro, spotlighting a detail, circular brand elements
transitions.effect: Focuses on the subject, then reveals the next scene.
transitions.prompt: Centred on B's subject, a circular mask grows from small to large to reveal B, 0.5 s.
transitions.pitfalls: The centre must match the visual focal point.

transitions.name: Clock Wipe
transitions.how: 1 Create a sector mask. 2 Rotate it open around the centre. 3 B is fully revealed after one full turn.
transitions.use_when: Timers, stage changes, graphic demos
transitions.effect: Implies time passing or a step completed.
transitions.prompt: Clockwise sector wipe from 12 o'clock reveals B, completing one turn in 0.6 s.
transitions.pitfalls: Keep the centre fixed.

transitions.name: Cube
transitions.how: 1 Map A and B onto adjacent faces of a cube. 2 Keep the camera fixed. 3 Rotate the cube 90° to reach B.
transitions.use_when: Feature modules, demo videos, retro digital visuals
transitions.effect: Emphasises a page or space flipping over.
transitions.prompt: Map A and B onto adjacent cube faces and rotate 90° to the left, 0.5 s.
transitions.pitfalls: This is a 3D effect on flat textures, not a real camera move through space.

transitions.name: Page Curl / Book Flip
transitions.how: 1 Treat A as a bendable page. 2 Animate the corner curl and shadow. 3 Reveal B underneath.
transitions.use_when: Photo albums, books, story chapters, education
transitions.effect: A sense of leafing through and looking back.
transitions.prompt: Turn A like a book page from right to left to reveal B, with a soft shadow, 0.7 s.
transitions.pitfalls: Page geometry and shadows must be consistent.

transitions.name: First–Last-Frame Spatial Bridge
transitions.how: 1 Take A's last frame and B's first frame. 2 Feed them to a model that supports first/last frames. 3 Describe a single motion path, then trim the seam after generation.
transitions.use_when: Flying through doorways, architectural spaces, fantasy ads
transitions.effect: Generates continuous spatial motion that the original footage doesn't have.
transitions.prompt: From A's last frame, move forward through the doorway, continuously advancing to B's first frame, with a steady camera.
transitions.duration: Generate 2–5 s, then pick a section
transitions.pitfalls: Duration depends on model support; check for structural warping and seam jumps.

transitions.name: Subject Morph
transitions.how: 1 Choose A and B subjects with similar silhouettes. 2 Provide first and last reference frames. 3 Lock background and camera, then generate the transformation.
transitions.use_when: Creative product concepts, surreal ads, music videos
transitions.effect: One subject continuously turns into another.
transitions.prompt: Locked camera; A's subject smoothly transforms into B's subject, keeping centre, lighting and background unchanged.
transitions.duration: Generate 2–5 s, then pick a section
transitions.pitfalls: Different from an interview Morph Cut; don't assume brand text will be preserved exactly.

transitions.name: Same-Composition Environment Change
transitions.how: 1 Lock subject position and camera. 2 Prepare old and new environment references. 3 Describe only the environment change, then check subject consistency.
transitions.use_when: Changing seasons, day to night, time passing in one place
transitions.effect: Keeps the visual anchor while changing time and place.
transitions.prompt: Fixed composition and subject; the environment changes continuously from A's daytime to B's night, with lighting shifting smoothly.
transitions.duration: Generate 2–5 s, then pick a section
transitions.pitfalls: Generative approaches are editorial suggestions; select results for consistency.
